text: When working with APIs, you send HTTP requests—like GET or POST—to a server to retrieve or send data. Most modern APIs return information in JSON format, which is easy for computers to read and organize. However, you usually need authentication first, often using an API key or a token, to prove you have permission to access the service. Once you start making calls, pay attention to rate limits, which stop you from sending too many requests in a short time. If you ignore them, the server may block you temporarily. Finally, always handle errors gracefully. Check the response status codes, such as 404 or 500, so your program can react calmly instead of crashing.
